xs-changes(7) ​

Changelog

What changed in each version, with links to the backlog stories behind each entry.

CHANGES ​

All notable changes to xsync (the xs executable). Story IDs refer to backlog.md, where each one has its verification evidence.

Unreleased — 0.1.0, protocol 4 ​

No release has been tagged yet. This section covers everything up to the current main.

Changed ​

  • The executable is now xs in every build, install and release (xs-linux-amd64, xs-linux-arm64, xs-darwin-universal). XSYNC_* environment variables and ~/.config/xsync/config keep their names. Diagnostics name the executable xs too, for example remote xs is not installed on HOST.
  • Native remote transfers use protocol 4 and still interoperate with protocol-3 peers. Optional capabilities are negotiated as feature bits instead of requiring equal versions (R-06).
  • New byte-copied files are written to a temporary name and renamed after verification by default; --no-atomic writes them directly (T-11).
  • Progress is shown by default when stderr is a terminal, and stays off in scripts; --no-progress and XSYNC_PROGRESS override it (U-06).

Added ​

  • Automatic fallback to a real rsync for unsupported options, daemon URLs and remote hosts without a compatible xs, with a one-line notice; --no-fallback and XSYNC_FALLBACK=0 for strict native runs (R-02).
  • Static release binaries for Linux amd64/arm64 and a macOS universal binary (R-03), explicit xs --install HOST (R-04), automatic helper lookup on the remote host (R-05), cmake --install with a generated manpage and zsh completion (R-07), IPv6 and unusual host specs (R-08), and personal defaults in XSYNC_OPTS and a config file (R-09).
  • Verified-prefix resume for -P/--partial (E-01); --out-format, --log-file and stable sorted script output (E-02); rsync-compatible itemization, including -ii (E-03).
  • Block-matching delta transfers for large changed files, locally and remotely (E-04).
  • Source listing and --list-only (E-05), and a bounded end-of-run error summary (E-06).
  • --bwlimit, --timeout and keep-alives (E-07).
  • Filter rule sides, merge files, -F, -C, --delete-after and -m (E-08).
  • --files-from, -R and -0 (E-09).
  • Metadata beyond -a: -H, -X, -A, -E, -U, -N, --fileflags, --chmod and --chown (E-10).
  • -S sparse files and --link-dest snapshots (E-11).
  • macOS dataless files, sockets and immutable files (E-12).
  • Prompt cancellation when stdout is closed, with exit 13 (E-13).
  • Calmer progress rows for small files (U-02), directory clone activity (U-03), receiver-acknowledged push progress (U-04), wire rate, compression ratio and the limiting stage (U-05), --info=progress2 and --progress=json (U-07), explicit phases such as deleting, verifying and waiting for receiver (U-08), dry-run plan summaries (U-09), one size-unit rule everywhere (U-10), and suspend/resume with cursor restoration on every exit path (U-11).
  • A product page and manual in sites/xsync, generated from the executable’s help, the source and captured output.

Fixed ​

  • Repeated syncs into a destination inside the source no longer nest without limit (T-01).
  • host:~/path and remote wildcards expand as with rsync (T-02, T-03).
  • Accepted-but-ignored options and silent attribute failures now fail or fall back visibly (T-04, T-05).
  • Files that change while being read are detected (T-06); --delete stops after source I/O errors (T-07); interrupted remote transfers clean up (T-08).
  • Disk-full handling, -x across mount points, case and Unicode name collisions, receiver symlink safety, Ctrl-C during remote transfers, and root-only paths are fixed and tested (T-09, T-10, T-12 to T-15).

Known gaps ​

  • Real-ssh end-to-end checks on every physical target are still partial (R-01). The manual terminal pass was skipped at the user’s request (U-01).
  • Performance work (P3) and the engineering base (P4) are open; see the backlog’s tier tables and sites/xsync’s development status page.

VERSIONS OF THIS MANUAL ​

No release has been tagged yet, so this manual describes the current main. When the first release is tagged, its manual will be kept under its own version, and this page will link to it.
